coaching:
**Strengths:**
1. Your posture score (100/100) meets professional standards. Maintaining good posture for the entire presentation improves perceived credibility (Toastmasters International - Using Body Language Guide).
2. Your eye contact proxy (100/100) aligns with the benchmark for professional speakers who maintain forward-facing gaze 85-95% of the time. This demonstrates confidence and trustworthiness (Overcoming Public Speaking Anxiety through Nonverbal Communication).

**Areas to Improve:**
1. Your gesture frequency (24.7/min) significantly exceeds the recommended range of 3-8 gestures per minute. This high frequency can appear frantic or nervous (GestureLens: Visual Analysis of Gestures in Presentation Videos).
2. Your engagement score (45/100) suggests limited torso/head movement. Aim for continuous subtle movement averaging 8-15% body normalized per minute to increase engagement (GestureLens - Temporal Distribution Analysis).
3. Your gesture quality score (58/100) indicates an over-reliance on one-handed or asymmetric gestures. Symmetric, bilateral gestures are perceived as more confident (GestureLens Research Paper - Spatial and Temporal Distribution Analysis).

**Evidence-Based Technique:**
Employ the "Gesture Box" technique: Keep gestures within a defined space between shoulders and waist, extending no further than elbow width from body. This creates natural, controlled movement that reinforces your message without distraction and will help lower your gesture frequency (How to Improve Non-Verbal Communication Skills: Master the 5 Core Elements).
